title: Decimals: The Four Operations
seo_title: Decimals – Primary 6 Mathematics Worksheets with Answers (NERDC)
standard_text: Add, subtract, multiply and divide decimals; multiply and divide by 10, 100 and 1,000; convert between fractions and decimals; solve word problems. (summary of the NERDC Primary 6 Mathematics curriculum)
meta_desc: Free Primary 6 maths worksheets on decimals: multiplying and dividing by powers of ten, adding, subtracting, multiplying and dividing decimals, and word problems. 100 questions with answers.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Line up the decimal points to add and subtract.
  • To multiply, multiply as whole numbers, then count the decimal places in the question: 0.4 × 0.3 = 0.12.
  • To divide by a decimal, multiply both numbers by 10 or 100 so that you divide by a whole number: 4.8 ÷ 0.6 = 48 ÷ 6 = 8.

Examples

Example

2.5 × 1.4

25 × 14 = 350

2 decimal places

Answer: 3.50 = 3.5

Example

7.2 ÷ 0.08

720 ÷ 8

Answer: 90

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Putting the point in the wrong placeCount the decimal places in the question.
Thinking multiplying always makes bigger× 0.5 halves a number.
Moving the point only in one numberWhen you divide, move the point in both numbers.

faq.q: Why do we multiply both numbers by 10 when dividing?
faq.a: It does not change the answer, but makes the divisor a whole number.
In money, measurements and sport times.

items.e: 4.6 ÷ 100: every digit moves 2 places to the right. The decimal point stays still. Write 0 in the empty places up to the units. 4.6 ÷ 100 = 0.046.
0.37 × 10: every digit moves 1 place to the left. The decimal point stays still. 0.37 × 10 = 3.7.
2.58 × 100: every digit moves 2 places to the left. The decimal point stays still. 2.58 × 100 = 258.
6.1 × 1,000: every digit moves 3 places to the left. The decimal point stays still. Write 0 in the empty places up to the units. 6.1 × 1,000 = 6,100.
52 ÷ 1,000: every digit moves 3 places to the right. The decimal point stays still. Write 0 in the empty places up to the units. 52 ÷ 1,000 = 0.052.
0.4 ÷ 10: every digit moves 1 place to the right. The decimal point stays still. Write 0 in the empty places up to the units. 0.4 ÷ 10 = 0.04.
0.008 × 100: every digit moves 2 places to the left. The decimal point stays still. 0.008 × 100 = 0.8.
309 ÷ 100: every digit moves 2 places to the right. The decimal point stays still. 309 ÷ 100 = 3.09.
7.25 ÷ 10: every digit moves 1 place to the right. The decimal point stays still. Write 0 in the empty places up to the units. 7.25 ÷ 10 = 0.725.
0.06 × 1,000: every digit moves 3 places to the left. The decimal point stays still. Write 0 in the empty places up to the units. 0.06 × 1,000 = 60.
13.4 ÷ 100: every digit moves 2 places to the right. The decimal point stays still. Write 0 in the empty places up to the units. 13.4 ÷ 100 = 0.134.
0.045 × 1,000: every digit moves 3 places to the left. The decimal point stays still. 0.045 × 1,000 = 45.
Use the inverse: 0.32 × 100. The digits move 2 places to the left: 32. Check: 32 ÷ 100 = 0.32.
The 4 moved from the units to the thousands: that is 3 places to the left, so the number is 1,000. (4.5 × 100 = 450.)
The 1 moved from the tens to the hundredths: that is 3 places to the right, so it is ÷ 1,000. (18 ÷ 100 = 0.18.)

items.q: Which calculation has the answer 0.63?
The chart shows 70.5 ÷ 100 = 0.705. What is the value of the red digit?
items.e: 70.5 ÷ 100 = 0.705. Every digit moved 2 places to the right, so the 5 is now in the thousandths place. Its value is 5 thousandths.

items.q: The chart shows 3.42 × 10 = 34.2. What is the value of the red digit?
items.e: 3.42 × 10 = 34.2. Every digit moved 1 place to the left, so the 4 is now in the ones place. Its value is 4 units.

items.q: The chart shows 86 ÷ 1,000 = 0.086. What is the value of the red digit?
items.e: 86 ÷ 1,000 = 0.086. Every digit moved 3 places to the right, so the 8 is now in the hundredths place. Its value is 8 hundredths.

items.q: The chart shows 0.29 × 100 = 29. What is the value of the red digit?
items.e: 0.29 × 100 = 29. Every digit moved 2 places to the left, so the 2 is now in the tens place. Its value is 2 tens.

items.q: Use column addition. The grey zeros fill the empty places.
items.e: Line up the decimal points. Write 2.6 as 2.60 so every place has a digit. 3.45 + 2.60 = 6.05.

items.e: Line up the decimal points. Write 12.5 as 12.50 so every place has a digit. 12.50 − 3.78 = 8.72. Check with the inverse: 8.72 + 3.78 = 12.5.

items.e: Line up the decimal points. Write 14.3 as 14.30 so every place has a digit. 14.30 + 2.95 = 17.25.

items.q: Ifeoma worked out 4.7 + 1.25 like this. What is the correct answer?
items.e: Ifeoma lined up the last digits, so the 7 tenths were added to 5 hundredths. Line up the decimal points: 4.70 + 1.25 = 5.95. (5.32 puts the 7 in the hundredths column.)
Line up the decimal points. Write 0.6 as 0.60 so every place has a digit. 0.75 + 0.60 = 1.35.
Line up the decimal points. Write 3.9 as 3.90 so every place has a digit. 6.07 + 3.90 = 9.97.
Line up the decimal points. Write 10 as 10.00 so every place has a digit. 10.00 − 4.62 = 5.38. Check with the inverse: 5.38 + 4.62 = 10.
Line up the decimal points. Write 5.3 as 5.30 so every place has a digit. 5.30 − 0.86 = 4.44. Check with the inverse: 4.44 + 0.86 = 5.3.
Line up the decimal points. Write 15 as 15.00 so every place has a digit. 15.00 − 6.25 = 8.75. Check with the inverse: 8.75 + 6.25 = 15.
Line up the decimal points. Write 4.2 as 4.200 so every place has a digit. 4.200 − 1.375 = 2.825. Check with the inverse: 2.825 + 1.375 = 4.2.
Line up the decimal points. Write 23.6 as 23.600 so every place has a digit. 23.600 + 8.475 = 32.075.
Line up the decimal points. Write 6.4 as 6.40 so every place has a digit. 6.40 − 1.27 = 5.13. Check with the inverse: 5.13 + 1.27 = 6.4.
Line up the decimal points. Write 0.9 as 0.90 so every place has a digit. 0.90 + 0.25 = 1.15.
Write 1 as 1.00. 1.00 − 0.37 = 0.63. Check: 0.37 + 0.63 = 1.00. The hundredths make 10, so the tenths only need to make 9. (0.73 makes each digit up to 10.)
Write 1 as 1.00. 1.00 − 0.45 = 0.55. Check: 0.55 + 0.45 = 1. (0.65 makes each digit up to 10, but the tenths only need to make 9.)
Line up the points and fill the empty places: 2.50 + 1.75 + 0.80. Hundredths: 5. Tenths: 5 + 7 + 8 = 20, write 0, exchange 2 units. Units: 2 + 1 + 0 + 2 = 5. Answer: 5.05.
Use the inverse: the missing number is 4.85 + 2.6. 4.85 + 2.60 = 7.45. Check: 7.45 − 2.6 = 4.85.
3 tenths × 4 = 12 tenths. 10 tenths make 1 unit, so 12 tenths = 1.2.
6 tenths × 5 = 30 tenths. 10 tenths make 1 unit, so 30 tenths = 3.
8 hundredths × 7 = 56 hundredths = 0.56.
4 hundredths × 3 = 12 hundredths. 10 hundredths make 1 tenth, so the answer is 0.12.
Tenths: 4 × 3 = 12. Write 2, exchange 1 unit. Units: 1 × 3 + 1 = 4. Write 4. The point goes straight below the point: 4.2.
Tenths: 6 × 4 = 24. Write 4, exchange 2 units. Units: 2 × 4 + 2 = 10. Write 10. The point goes straight below the point: 10.4.
Tenths: 7 × 6 = 42. Write 2, exchange 4 units. Units: 3 × 6 + 4 = 22. Write 22. The point goes straight below the point: 22.2.
Tenths: 8 × 7 = 56. Write 6, exchange 5 units. Units: 5 × 7 + 5 = 40. Write 40. The point goes straight below the point: 40.6.

items.q: Use short multiplication. What is 2.45 × 6?
items.e: Hundredths: 5 × 6 = 30. Write 0, exchange 3 tenths. Tenths: 4 × 6 + 3 = 27. Write 7, exchange 2 units. Units: 2 × 6 + 2 = 14. Write 14. The point goes straight below the point: 14.70 = 14.7.

items.q: Use short multiplication. What is 1.36 × 4?
items.e: Hundredths: 6 × 4 = 24. Write 4, exchange 2 tenths. Tenths: 3 × 4 + 2 = 14. Write 4, exchange 1 unit. Units: 1 × 4 + 1 = 5. Write 5. The point goes straight below the point: 5.44.

items.q: Use short multiplication. What is 3.25 × 8?
items.e: Hundredths: 5 × 8 = 40. Write 0, exchange 4 tenths. Tenths: 2 × 8 + 4 = 20. Write 0, exchange 2 units. Units: 3 × 8 + 2 = 26. Write 26. The point goes straight below the point: 26.00 = 26.

items.q: Use short multiplication. What is 4.07 × 5?
items.e: Hundredths: 7 × 5 = 35. Write 5, exchange 3 tenths. Tenths: 0 × 5 + 3 = 3. Write 3. Units: 4 × 5 = 20. Write 20. The point goes straight below the point: 20.35.

items.q: Use short multiplication. What is 6.78 × 3?
items.e: Hundredths: 8 × 3 = 24. Write 4, exchange 2 tenths. Tenths: 7 × 3 + 2 = 23. Write 3, exchange 2 units. Units: 6 × 3 + 2 = 20. Write 20. The point goes straight below the point: 20.34.

items.q: Use short multiplication. What is 9.15 × 4?
items.e: Hundredths: 5 × 4 = 20. Write 0, exchange 2 tenths. Tenths: 1 × 4 + 2 = 6. Write 6. Units: 9 × 4 = 36. Write 36. The point goes straight below the point: 36.60 = 36.6.

items.q: 136 × 4 = 544. Use this to work out 1.36 × 4.

items.e: 0.37 is 37 ÷ 100, so 0.37 × 6 = 222 ÷ 100 = 2.22. Estimate: 0.37 is less than a half, and half of 6 is 3, so the answer is less than 3.
Partition 12 into 10 and 2. 0.75 × 10 = 7.5 and 0.75 × 2 = 1.5. 7.5 + 1.5 = 9. (7.5 forgets the 0.75 × 2 part. Or: three quarters of 12 is 9.)
Partition 25 into 20 and 5. 4.6 × 20 = 92 and 4.6 × 5 = 23. 92 + 23 = 115. (92 forgets the 4.6 × 5 part.)

items.q: Which is the best estimate for 3.92 × 7?
items.e: Round 3.92 to the nearest whole number: 4. Then 4 × 7 = 28. The exact answer is 27.44.

items.q: Which calculation has the same answer as 2.45 × 6?
Use short division. What is 8.4 ÷ 4?
items.e: 8 ÷ 4 = 2; 4 ÷ 4 = 1. Keep the point in line: 8.4 ÷ 4 = 2.1.

items.q: Use short division. What is 9.36 ÷ 3?
Use short division. What is 7.38 ÷ 6?
Use short division. What is 4.08 ÷ 4?
17 ÷ 4 = ? Give your answer as a decimal.
items.e: Write 17 as 17.00 (the grey zeros). 17 ÷ 4 = 4 r 1. Exchange the 1 for 10 tenths: 10 ÷ 4 = 2 r 2. Exchange the 2 tenths for 20 hundredths: 20 ÷ 4 = 5. Answer: 4.25. (4.1 writes the remainder 1 as a decimal, but r 1 means 1 left over out of 4, which is 0.25.)
2 ÷ 8 = 0 r 2; 24 ÷ 8 = 3. Keep the point in line: 2.4 ÷ 8 = 0.3.

items.q: 13 ÷ 5 = ? Give your answer as a decimal.
items.e: Write 13 as 13.0 so you can keep dividing. 13 ÷ 5 = 2 r 3; 30 ÷ 5 = 6. Keep the point in line: 13 ÷ 5 = 2.6. (Not 2.3: the remainder is not the decimal part.)

items.q: 23 ÷ 4 = ? Give your answer as a decimal.
items.e: Write 23 as 23.00 so you can keep dividing. 23 ÷ 4 = 5 r 3; 30 ÷ 4 = 7 r 2; 20 ÷ 4 = 5. Keep the point in line: 23 ÷ 4 = 5.75. (Not 5.3: the remainder is not the decimal part.)

items.q: Both decimal points move the same number of places. What is 4.56 ÷ 0.12?
items.e: 0.12 has 2 decimal places, so multiply both numbers by 100 (move both points 2 places right). 4.56 ÷ 0.12 = 456 ÷ 12 = 38. Check: 38 × 0.12 = 4.56.

items.q: Both decimal points move the same number of places. What is 1.5 ÷ 0.25?
items.e: 0.25 has 2 decimal places, so multiply both numbers by 100 (move both points 2 places right) and write a zero in 1.5. 1.5 ÷ 0.25 = 150 ÷ 25 = 6. Check: 6 × 0.25 = 1.5.

items.q: Both decimal points move the same number of places. What is 2.24 ÷ 0.7?
items.e: 0.7 has 1 decimal place, so multiply both numbers by 10 (move both points 1 place right). 2.24 ÷ 0.7 = 22.4 ÷ 7 = 3.2. Check: 3.2 × 0.7 = 2.24.

items.q: Both decimal points move the same number of places. What is 0.63 ÷ 0.009?
items.e: 0.009 has 3 decimal places, so multiply both numbers by 1,000 (move both points 3 places right) and write a zero in 0.63. 0.63 ÷ 0.009 = 630 ÷ 9 = 70. Check: 70 × 0.009 = 0.63.

items.q: Which problem has the same quotient as 7.35 ÷ 0.5?
items.e: 0.5 has 1 decimal place, so multiply both numbers by 10: 7.35 → 73.5 and 0.5 → 5. 7.35 ÷ 0.5 = 73.5 ÷ 5 = 14.7. Move the point the same number of places in both numbers.

items.q: Which problem has the same quotient as 0.18 ÷ 0.006?
items.e: 0.006 has 3 decimal places, so multiply both numbers by 1,000: 0.18 → 180 and 0.006 → 6. 0.18 ÷ 0.006 = 180 ÷ 6 = 30. Move the point the same number of places in both numbers.

items.q: Which problem has the same quotient as 12 ÷ 0.75?
items.e: 0.75 has 2 decimal places, so multiply both numbers by 100: 12 → 1,200 and 0.75 → 75. 12 ÷ 0.75 = 1,200 ÷ 75 = 16. Move the point the same number of places in both numbers.
0.8 has 1 decimal place, so multiply both numbers by 10 (move both points 1 place right). 9.6 ÷ 0.8 = 96 ÷ 8 = 12. Check: 12 × 0.8 = 9.6.
0.12 has 2 decimal places, so multiply both numbers by 100 (move both points 2 places right). 0.144 ÷ 0.12 = 14.4 ÷ 12 = 1.2. Check: 1.2 × 0.12 = 0.144.
1.5 has 1 decimal place, so multiply both numbers by 10 (move both points 1 place right). 3.75 ÷ 1.5 = 37.5 ÷ 15 = 2.5. Check: 2.5 × 1.5 = 3.75.

items.q: Usman has 6.75 m of ribbon. He cuts it into pieces 0.45 m long. How many pieces does he get?
One lap of a track is 0.4 km. Funke runs 7.5 laps. How far does she run?
items.e: Multiply: 7.5 × 0.4. 75 × 4 = 300, and 1 + 1 = 2 decimal places give 3.00 = 3 km. (7.9 km is the sum.)

items.q: Zainab runs 5 km in 27.5 minutes at a steady pace. How many minutes does each kilometre take?
items.e: Divide: 27.5 ÷ 5. 275 ÷ 5 = 55, and the point goes above the point: 5.5 minutes. Check: 5 × 5.5 = 27.5. (22.5 subtracts.)

items.q: One batch of granola needs 0.75 cup of honey. Simi makes 2.5 batches. How much honey does she need?
items.e: Multiply: 2.5 × 0.75. 25 × 75 = 1,875, and 1 + 2 = 3 decimal places give 1.875 cups. (3.25 is the sum.)

items.q: Each lap of the pool takes Chioma 1.25 minutes. She swims for 15 minutes. How many laps does she swim?
items.e: Divide: 15 ÷ 1.25. Move both points 2 places: 1,500 ÷ 125 = 12. Check: 12 × 1.25 = 15. (18.75 multiplies.)

items.q: A tank holds 37.8 L of water. How many 0.6 L bottles can be filled from it?
Joy wants to bike 30 km this week. She rides 12.6 km on Monday and 8.75 km on Tuesday. How many more kilometres does she need to ride?
items.e: Step 1: 12.60 + 8.75 = 21.35 km so far. Step 2: 30.00 − 21.35 = 8.65 km. (21.35 km is the distance already ridden. 19.99 km comes from lining up the last digits.)

items.q: Tolu has 4.8 m of fabric. Each costume needs 0.75 m. How many costumes can she make, and how much fabric is left?
items.e: 4.8 ÷ 0.75 = 480 ÷ 75 = 6.4, so only 6 whole costumes fit. They use 6 × 0.75 = 4.5 m, and 4.8 − 4.5 = 0.3 m is left. (0.4 m reads the .4 of 6.4 as metres, but 0.4 of a costume is 0.4 × 0.75 = 0.3 m.)
